answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 자리: This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork.에서 'is shown'의 수일치나 태를 묻거나 동격 명사구 수식을 묻는다. 여기서는 'is shown'을 'showing' 혹은 능동 'shows'로 만들어 오답화한다. 아니면 'remained in Santa Fe, where he worked'에서 'where'를 'which'로 바꾼다. 'where' 자리를 'which'로 변형하여 뒷문장이 완전한데 관계대명사를 쓴 비문을 구성한다.

answer.surroundingText: Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist.

answerStage.explanation: 밑줄 친 which 뒷부분을 보면 'he(주어) worked(동사) as a freelance artist(수식어)'로 문장 구성 성분을 모두 갖춘 완전한 절이 이어지고 있습니다. 따라서 장소를 나타내는 선행사 Santa Fe를 수식하면서 완전한 절을 이끌 수 있는 관계부사 where(또는 in which)를 써야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 문장의 주어 he에 연결되는 단순과거 시제의 정동사로, 문맥상 과거의 사실을 서술하므로 형식이 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 주격 관계대명사인 that의 선행사가 단수인 an attachment이므로, 단수 동사 is shown으로 수일치를 맞춘 것은 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 디자인(Houser's designs)이 뿌리를 내리게 된(be rooted in) 수동의 상태를 서술하므로, 과거분사인 rooted가 적절하게 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): '~와 상관없이'라는 뜻의 전치사구 'regardless of'를 이끄는 형용사로, 문맥상 어법과 의미 모두 올바르게 사용되었습니다.

question.explanation: 밑줄 친 (C)의 which 다음 구성을 살펴보면, 'he(주어) worked(동사) as a freelance artist(수식어)'로 필수 성분을 모두 갖춘 완전한 절이 이어지고 있습니다. 따라서 장소를 나타내는 선행사 Santa Fe를 수식하면서 뒤에 완전한 절을 이끌 수 있는 관계부사인 where를 써야 올바른 문장이 됩니다. 관계대명사인 which는 불완전한 절을 이끌기 때문에 이 자리에서는 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 which를 where(또는 in which)로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (C) 관계대명사 vs 관계부사 — 관계사 뒤에 이어지는 문장 구조의 완전·불완전 여부로 판정
(B) 수일치 — 관계대명절 내의 주어 역할을 하는 선행사의 단/복수 여부 판정
(D) 분사구문 및 태 — 의미상 주어인 사물이 전통에 단단히 '뿌리 박힌' 수동 상태 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he __(A) listened__ to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that __(B) is shown__ in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, __(C) which__ he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly __(D) rooted__ in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, __(E) regardless__ of his or her background.

passageText: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장 인용: Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. 오류 변형: immersed -> immersing (c). 지각동사 see의 목적어 someone else가 '몰입된' 상태이므로 수동의 의미인 과거분사가 적절하다. 이를 현재분사로 바꾸면 목적어가 누군가를 몰입시킨다는 능동의 의미가 되므로 문맥상 비문이 된다.

answer.surroundingText: Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all.

answerStage.explanation: 지각동사 see의 목적어인 someone else가 책이나 활동에 '몰입된' 상태를 나타내므로 수동의 의미를 지닌 과거분사 immersed가 목적격 보어로 와야 합니다. 목적어가 누군가를 몰입시키는 능동의 주체가 아니므로 현재분사 immersing은 문맥상 어색한 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 immersing을 과거분사 immersed로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 전치사의 목적어 자리에 동명사가 오면서, 주어인 we가 혼자 '남겨지는' 수동의 상태를 나타내므로 수동형 동명사 being left는 어법상 자연스럽습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 선행사인 선행사 other people을 수식하며, 관계절 안에서 주어 역할을 하는 주격 관계대명사이므로 이 자리에 who가 쓰인 것은 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 선행사 a reading group 뒤에서 '전치사+관계대명사' 구조를 이룹니다. 뒷부분이 주어(everybody), 동사(takes), 목적어로 완전한 절이 이어지고 있으므로 올바른 표현입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 문장의 주어 핵이 동명사인 Reading이므로, 3인칭 단수 주어에 수일치하여 단수 동사 is로 받는 것은 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 이 문장은 지각동사 see와 목적어 someone else, 그리고 목적격 보어로 이어지는 구조를 가집니다. 목적어인 someone else가 무언가를 몰입시키는 능동의 행위자가 아니라 특정한 활동에 '몰입된' 수동의 상태이므로 목적격 보어 자리에 현재분사 immersing을 쓰는 것은 비문입니다. 따라서 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 immersed로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (C) 분사의 능동 vs 수동 — 지각동사의 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 수동이므로 과거분사 사용
(A) 동명사의 태 — 전치사 뒤에서 동명사의 의미상 주어와의 수동 관계 판단
(D) 관계부사 대용의 전치사+관계사 — 뒤에 완전한 격을 갖춘 절이 오는지 확인
question.passageWithMarkers: We all enjoy the pleasure of __(A) being left__ alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people __(B) who__ are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly __(C) immersing__, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group __(D) in which__ everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively __(E) is__ a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

passageText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 자리: 'We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie.'에서 'responsible'을 수식하는 분사의 능동/수동으로 오해할 만한 자리를 찾거나 동사의 정/준동사 자리를 찾는다. 하지만 원문을 보면 'qualifies'라는 동사가 'a thousand lines of letters in UNIX' 뒤에 오며, 주어가 'a thousand lines...'로 보이지만 'lines'로 볼 수도 있고 의미상 'a block of code'로 취급되기 때문에 단수 'qualifies'를 썼다. 다른 부분에서, 'The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures.'에서 'is' 자리를 정동사/준동사(a) 포인트로 낸다. 정동사 is를 being으로 바꾸어 심으면, 문장의 본동사가 없어져 비문이 된다. 반증: 분사구문으로 볼 여지도 없다(마침표로 끝나는 완전한 문장).

answer.surroundingText: The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures.

answerStage.explanation: 이 문장은 'The literary rendering of the original novel'을 주어로 삼고 있습니다. 따라서 이 주어의 상태나 정체를 설명하는 정동사가 필요합니다. 'being'을 사용하면 문장 내에 본동사가 없게 되어 어법상 틀린 문장(비문)이 됩니다. 그러므로 주어의 단수 형태에 맞추어 정동사 'is'로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They are something useful produced by a mind.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 동사 acknowledge의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 that으로, 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어지므로 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 조동사 can에 연결되는 동사원형의 병렬 구조(change, alter, or enable)로서 어법상 올바른 형태입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 수식받는 명사 something과 동사 produce가 수동 관계이므로 과거분사 produced를 사용한 것은 어법상 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 앞에 있는 명사 multiple overlapping technologies를 뒤에서 수식하는 형용사구의 핵심 형용사로서 responsible의 쓰임이 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 이 문장의 진짜 주어 핵(head)은 수식어구 'of the original novel'의 수식을 받는 명사 'rendering'입니다. 주어 핵이 단수이므로 동사도 단수형이어야 합니다. 따라서 복수 동사 'are'는 어법상 틀리며, 'is'로 고쳐야 합니다. 동사 앞의 복수형태 명사(novel 등)에 시선을 뺏기지 않도록 문장 구조를 분석하는 것이 중요합니다.
keyPoints: (E) 주어-동사 수일치 — 수식어를 걷어낸 진짜 주어 핵 파악
(A) 명사절 접속사 that vs 관계대명사 what — 뒤 문장의 완전성과 역할 파악
(C) 분사 구문의 능수동 — 수식받는 명사와의 능수동 관계 파악
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge __(A) that__ technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or __(B) enable__ future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful __(C) produced__ by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies __(D) responsible__ for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel __(E) are__ as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

passageText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful produced by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 자리: 'train yourself to acknowledge'에서 동사 train. 이를 분사 training으로 바꾸면 주절의 정동사가 없어져 비문이 됩니다. 부정적 편향에서 벗어나기 위해 스스로를 훈련하라는 명령문 구조이므로 정동사가 필요합니다.

answer.surroundingText: To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right.

answerStage.explanation: 문장의 주절에 해당하는 부분으로, 주어 없이 동사원형으로 시작하는 명령문 구조가 되어야 합니다. 따라서 준동사인 training이 아니라 정동사인 train이 와야 합니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime).

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling).

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주어인 The human brain이 수동의 대상이 되어 프로그래밍되어 있다는 의미이므로, 수동태인 is wired가 올바르게 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 앞선 문장 혹은 구의 내용을 선행사로 받아 부연 설명을 이어가는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사이므로 which가 적절하게 사용되었습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 전치사 by의 목적어 자리이므로, 동명사(v-ing) 형태인 sharing이 올바르게 구조를 이룹니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 앞서 언급된 명사인 life(삶)를 지칭하므로, 단수 대명사 it이 올바르게 사용되었습니다.

question.explanation: 부사구 인 'To break out of this neural rut' 다음에 이어지는 주절에 해당하는 부분으로, 주어 없이 동사 본연의 형태로 문장을 시작하는 명령문의 구조를 취해야 합니다. 어법상 정동사 자리이므로 준동사인 training이 쓰일 수 없습니다. 따라서 주절을 완결할 수 있도록 문맥상 동사원형인 train으로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (C) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 부사구 이후 문장 전체를 완결할 주절의 정동사(명령문) 필요성 판단
(B) 관계대명사 계속적 용법 — 앞 문장의 내용 일부(혹은 전체)를 선행사로 취할 때의 올바른 연결

passageText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

passageText: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

passageText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. (B) 현재분사 vs 과거분사 — 의미상 주어와의 능수동 관계로 판정
(A) 동사의 수일치 — 주격 관계결에서 선행사를 파악하여 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: There is a critical factor that __(A) determines__ whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found __(B) strolling__ in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, __(C) where__ likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that __(D) occurs__, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer __(E) survives__, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

passageText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장 인용: 'Consistency always brings better results.' 오류 변형: brings → bringing. 문장의 주어인 Consistency 뒤에 문장을 완결할 술어 동사(정동사)가 필요한 자리이다. bringing은 준동사이므로 단독으로 본동사 역할을 할 수 없어 명백한 비문이 된다. 다른 해석으로 보아 분사구문으로 취급하려 해도 주절이 존재하지 않아 비문이 된다.
answerStage.explanation: 주어인 'Consistency'에 이어지는 문장의 본동사가 필요한 자리입니다. 준동사인 현재분사나 동명사 형태인 'bringing'은 단독으로 문장의 술어 동사 역할을 할 수 없으므로 어법상 틀립니다. 단수 주어와 현재 시제에 맞게 정동사인 'brings'로 고쳐야 합니다.

wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 문장의 주어인 'relationships'가 유지하는 행위의 대상이므로, 수동 형태인 'aren't kept up'을 쓴 것은 어법상 옳습니다.

question.explanation: 문장의 주어인 'Consistency'에 이어지는 절의 본동사(정동사)가 필요한 위치입니다. 그러나 'bringing'과 같은 현재분사(준동사) 형태는 단독으로 술어 동사의 역할을 할 수 없으므로 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 3인칭 단수 주어와 현재 시제를 나타낼 수 있는 정동사인 'brings'로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (E) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 한 문장 내에서 본동사(술어)의 누락 여부를 판단하여 수일치가 적용된 정동사로 판정
(B) 분사구문의 능수동 — 의미상 주어와의 능동 관계를 확인하여 현재분사형으로 판정
(D) 대명사 vs 재귀대명사 — 의미상 주어와 목적어가 가리키는 대상이 동일하므로 재귀대명사로 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance __(A) that__ has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, __(B) hoping__ that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships __(C) aren't kept up__ with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let __(D) yourself__ fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always __(E) bringing__ better results.

passageText: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.
